storyTagline: Skura's first season in Philadelphia ends with Super Bowl CXLVII, a record debut for Bones Crawford, a third OPOY for Vyncint Heath and two new Hall of Famers.

stories.headline: Philadelphia Rises: Skura Takes the Eagles to the Super Bowl CXLVII Title
stories.dek: In his first season in Philadelphia, Dorren Skura led the Eagles to a 14-2-1 record, past Atlanta and Green Bay, and to a 40-22 win over the Broncos.

stories.headline: Bones Crawford Arrives With 69 Touchdown Passes and a Super Bowl MVP
stories.dek: The Eagles quarterback put up one of the great debut cards in league history: 5,922 yards in 20 games.

stories.headline: Heath for Adam: The Receiver Swap That Shaped the Season
stories.dek: Philadelphia sent Apollo Adam to Atlanta for Vyncint Heath, and Heath answered with a third Offensive Player of the Year award.

stories.headline: Spector Scores 35 in Houston After the Ogbah Trade
stories.dek: The Eagles moved Siran Spector to the Texans for Gerrit Ogbah. Both backs had good years, and both teams can claim the deal.

stories.headline: The Falcons Run Ends Where the Coach Went
stories.dek: Atlanta still had Ryland Maxwell and a playoff team. It did not have Skura, and its run of titles ended in Philadelphia.

stories.headline: Toohill Wins a Second MVP and Brooker Takes Defensive Honors
stories.dek: Green Bay collected two of the season's biggest awards before the Eagles ended its year in the playoffs.

stories.headline: McClain and Orzech: Two One-Club Linemen Enter the Hall
stories.dek: The 49ers and Cowboys defensive linemen both crossed Career Legacy 7,500, and McClain sits one tackle from a record.

stories.headline: Diggs Passes 20,000 Yards and Takes the Rushing Touchdown Lead
stories.dek: The Jaguars back now has more rushing touchdowns than anyone on a card and is closing on Ikarras for yards.

stories.headline: A Champion Built on New Cards
stories.dek: Rahman, Shaheed and Brock joined Crawford as first-time cards on the title team, and Cairo Colbert arrived with a long career already behind him.
